text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered alert for tenant QuorraPay — reserved pool `rq-prod-eu-1`
alert: reserved_pool_latency_p95 > 5s (current p95=7.2s), 5xx_rate=8% over last 5m. Auto-fallback: queued to hosted fallback pool. PD Incident: INC1234567 :rotating_light: https://pagerduty.example/INC1234567

pagerduty-bot: Notification sent to escalation policy `eng-oncall`. Primary: alex (oncall). Auto-ack false — awaiting ack.

alex (oncall): Acked INC1234567 on PD, jumping in. First pass: is this tenant traffic spike or infra saturation? Jo, can you pull the reserved pool metrics?

jo (sre): pulling metrics now — seeing CPU on pool nodes at ~82%, mem stable. KV cache evictions for tenant keyspace up 4x. Sequence lengths up a bit. Looks like persistent requests from a single customer job causing KV fragmentation + long seqs. p95 latency spike aligns with kv-evict spikes. Log snippet:```
[2026-03-15T10:22:03Z] rq-prod-eu-1 - tenant=QuorraPay request_id=abcd1234 status=502 latency=7.1s cause=kv-miss
[2026-03-15T10:22:08Z] rq-prod-eu-1 - tenant=QuorraPay kv_evictions=128 active_kv_keys=12k
```

lee (infra): If it's kv pressure and node CPU nearing 85% we can scale the reserved pool (+2 replicas) or trigger tenant failover to their backup pool. Which do you want, Alex? Scaling will take ~90s to warm. Failover will route some traffic and may increase latency for a bit.

alex (oncall): Scale first. If error rate doesn't drop in 3m, failover to backup pool `rq-prod-eu-1b`. Jo — while scaling, can you try targeted cache eviction for QuorraPay prefixes to free KV memory?

jo (sre): Running targeted eviction now. Command:```
redwoodctl kv evict --tenant QuorraPay --prefix "session:" --force
```
Started run at 10:23:12Z. Also lowering model batch size for QuorraPay route to reduce per-token compute:```
redwoodctl route update --tenant QuorraPay --route /v1/generate --batch-max 4
```

lee (infra): Scaling reserved pool: executing:```
redwoodctl reserved scale --pool rq-prod-eu-1 --tenant QuorraPay --add-replicas 2 --reason "PD: latency spike"
```
Command accepted, rollout started at 10:23:25Z. Estimated warmup 60-120s. deploy-bot: rolling new nodes, watching health checks.

support-maya: @tina (acct) I'm pinging QuorraPay on the support channel, telling them we're aware and doing mitigation. Will ask if they deployed anything unusual.

tina (acct): noted. I'm DMing their technical contact and flagging this as impacting production traffic and SLA. Will update if they report a deploy.

alex (oncall): Good. Jo — any immediate config we can toggle to reduce 502s while nodes come up? Maybe increase soft-failover thresholds to avoid failing requests while hitting KV misses.

jo (sre): Pushed a short-lived route tolerance change:```
redwoodctl route set-tolerance --tenant QuorraPay --route /v1/generate --soft_fail_threshold 0.6 --duration 5m
```
This gives more perf headroom; watch for correctness regressions.

[10:24:45Z] deploy-bot: 2 new replicas for rq-prod-eu-1 are healthy and joined the pool.

alex (oncall): Monitoring metrics... p95 dropped to 3.4s, 5xx down to 1.2% after scaling + evict. Nice. Keep monitoring for 15m. If error rate rises above 3% re-open page and we failover.

support-maya: QuorraPay replied — they had a batch job restarting every minute, increasing concurrent long requests. They've paused it after our note.

tina (acct): Customer acknowledges mitigation. They'll coordinate with their SREs to change that job pattern.

jo (sre): Leaving the reduced batch size and soft-fail tolerance for 10m, then grad restore. Also setting an alert to notify if kv_evictions_per_min > 50 for this tenant.

incident-bot: Updating PD incident INC1234567: status=acknowledged, mitigation in progress, assigned to Alex. Next check-in in 10m.

alex (oncall): I'll close the Slack thread once we're stable for 15m. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

[10:36:30Z] alex (oncall): Confirming last check: p95=2.9s, 5xx=0.4%, kv_evictions back to baseline. Closing incident. If anything flares, reopen PD.

incident-bot: PD INC1234567 marked resolved by alex (oncall) at 10:36:30Z. Summary: scaled reserved pool +2, targeted kv prefix eviction, reduced route batch size, customer paused noisy job. Customer impact: elevated latency and some 502s for ~13m. Postmortem suggested.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved and auto-archived.
